decisions.executionNote: Approach the near side of the set square with both arms in their own workspaces; lower gradually while checking clearance.
Reduce increments after the continuity rejection; begin a gentle elbow-up approach without touching the blocks.
Close empty grippers and lower behind the tool, moving toward its two ends. Keep the square and cubes on the tabletop.
Replan from the executed prefix with smaller sideways motion and a shallow forward/down approach, preserving the current wrist configuration.
Change approach by gently pitching the grippers toward the tabletop, with only millimeter forward increments to maintain IK continuity.
Pitch the closed fingertips down while positioning behind separate ends of the square; stay above the table during reorientation.
Continue pitching and lowering toward the near edge, keeping the left contact slightly farther forward to match the square's initial slant.
Probe the square gently at tabletop height, advancing the right contact more to reduce the tool's slant. Watch for actual tool motion.
The square has not visibly moved. Back off slightly and lower the fingertips to engage its side instead of passing above it.
Keep the left contact steady and move the right gripper back to the near side before trying a controlled forward sweep.
The right end moved with contact. Reverse into a slow forward push while the left end stays steady, beginning to level the square.
The right fingers appear on the far side of the tool. Lift that empty gripper and retreat before re-engaging from behind; keep the left contact still.
Move the raised right fingertips behind the square's displaced near edge, then begin lowering without disturbing the cubes.
Lower the right fingertips beside the near face to the established contact height; keep both blocks and square resting on the table.
Both fingertips now visually meet the near face. Push the right end forward at fixed height to straighten the set square.
The square is now sliding forward under the right contact. Continue leveling its long edge before sweeping all three cubes.
Fine-level the square's edge before the common forward sweep; keep contact height fixed and do not grasp any cube.
Sweep both ends forward together at constant height, using the now-horizontal square to bring the nearer cubes toward the farthest cube's row.
Continue the level tabletop sweep until the square reaches the farthest cube and squares all three against the same straight edge.
All three cubes now appear in one row. Apply a final short, level seating push to make their faces parallel before withdrawing and resetting.
Withdraw both empty fingertips backward and slightly upward from the square, leaving the aligned cubes undisturbed; begin returning to the initial arm poses.
The cubes remain aligned after separation. Open the empty grippers and return both arms toward their initial positions and level wrist orientations with continuous elbow-up motion.
Continue the unobstructed reset toward the recorded starting poses, easing the wrists back to horizontal while keeping the aligned row untouched.
